summary: Round 1 raised 12 findings, round 2 raised 7 (including a self-correction that my round-1 fix for finding 5 was inert), round 3 verified all 19 fixed and raised 5 more. Every one was actioned; none deferred or argued away.

review.finding: F7 fallback predicate was WIDER than the canonical one and the docstring cited track_tool_calls.py falsely; a bare .shipwright/ would have spent three authenticated gh calls on a stranger's repository.
review.resolution: fixed - fallback is now a strict subset (run_config/build_config, .is_file()); docstring corrected; test forces the ImportError with monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, 'lib.project_root', None) and pins both directions.

review.finding: Unthrottled network producer on SessionStart, while the cited precedent (import_github_findings.py) IS throttled - the throttle is what makes a network call acceptable in a chain that runs before the session opens.
review.resolution: fixed - 6h throttle with run-config/env/default resolution mirroring github_triage/state.py; reserve-before-launch; 15 tests.

review.finding: TIMEOUT_SECONDS=45 wrong in both directions: below the producer's 210s worst case and ABOVE the 30s cap test_hook_output_schema_compliance puts on the whole chain.
review.resolution: fixed - 20s, silent on timeout; the tautological '> 0' assertion replaced with '0 < TIMEOUT_SECONDS <= 30' naming the chain cap.

review.finding: main() called resolve_project_root() outside run()'s guard; PermissionError/FileNotFoundError from Path.cwd()/iterdir() would produce the traceback and non-zero exit the design exists to prevent.
review.resolution: fixed - guarded, with a test that raises PermissionError through the resolver.

review.finding: The PowerShell missing-uv fix was INERT. CommandNotFoundException is statement-terminating, so the $LASTEXITCODE comparison never executes and no seeded value is ever read; the reviewer corrected its own round-1 mechanism claim to establish this.
review.resolution: fixed - $global:LASTEXITCODE reset deleted; Get-Command uv precondition + catch re-raising + finally Pop-Location; prose rewritten to the real mechanism; test asserts the precondition.

review.finding: Two subprocess tests did not pin SHIPWRIGHT_PROJECT_ROOT, so they could run the live chain against the developer's REAL repository - three authenticated gh calls and a real card written into their tree - and still pass.
review.resolution: fixed - _pinned_env() sets it (and shortens the throttle); the same one-line exposure closed in test_hook_output_schema_compliance.py, which affects the sibling producer too.

review.finding: _git_only_path() narrowed PATH to git's own directory, which isolates gh on Windows but NOT on ubuntu-latest where both are /usr/bin - so in CI the test would reach api.github.com and pass for the wrong reason.
review.resolution: fixed - git is copied into an empty fixture dir and PATH set to that; shutil.which('gh', path=...) is None asserted as a precondition so any future degradation is loud.

review.finding: Six further low findings: vacuous leak assertion; a tautological assertion; getattr-default-0; Path(str()) round-trip; wall-clock-dependent throttle test; run-config throttle source missing; asymmetric now= seam; _warn unguarded (re-entrancy into main()'s handler); future lastRun meaning permanent silence; catch wording reporting a FAILED gate as 'could not be run'.
review.resolution: all fixed. _warn guarded; is_due returns True on a future stamp; catch wording widened to 'did not pass'; run-config source implemented rather than documented away.

review.finding: Wrapper reached 299/300 by deleting prose, and the spec had used the identical 518/518 measurement to reject another placement.
review.resolution: fixed by extraction - throttle/outcome state moved to shared/scripts/hooks/required_checks_state.py (157 lines), wrapper down to ~274.
